nodes.question: What can the digestate obtained after digestion be used for?
nodes.answer: The digestate can be used as a bio-based fertilizer to recycle nutrients back to agricultural fields.
nodes.paragraph: (1234567890) combined heat and power production (CHP) in CHP units or can be purified into biomethane, which can be used in the gas grid for natural gas or in gas pow - ered vehicles (Hakawati et al. 2017; Scarlat et al. 2018). The upgrading to transport fuel offers an envi- ronmentally favorable alternative compared to com- bustion in CHP units (Styles et al. 2016). Nutrients in the organic input material are mostly retained in the residue after digestion, the digestate, which can be used as a bio-based fertilizer to recycle nutrients back to agricultural fields. The recent expansion of biogas production across Europe (Gustafsson & Anderberg 2022) has resulted in a lack of energy-rich feedstocks such as slaughterhouse waste. Potential supple- mentary feedstocks for biogas production which are receiving growing interest are cover crops (Feng et al. 2020). Cover crops are grown to reduce leaching of nutri- ents and soil erosion when there is no main crop in the field, i.e. in the time between main crops, mostly dur - ing autumn and winter.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Sustainable fertilizer use_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does fertilization with digestate affect nitrogen uptake efficiency for crops?
nodes.answer: Fertilization with digestate increases the share of directly plant-available nitrogen, improving nitrogen uptake efficiency, thereby contributing to better yields and reducing nitrogen losses to the environment.
nodes.paragraph: Fertilization with digestate could thus increase the share of directly plant-available N, which can be field applied at the right time to meet crop demand (Fon- taine et al. 2020a, b; M ller & M ller 2012). This could increase the N uptake efficiency, contributing to improved yields and lower losses of N to the envi- ronment (DCE 2021; Fr seth et al. 2014). Harvesting of cover crops could also lead to avoided emissions from their decomposition in the field, such as ammo- nia and nitrous oxide (Fr seth et al. 2014; Nadeem et al. 2012), and leaching of nitrate, which can take place when nitrate is released at times of low crop demand (DCE 2021). The harvesting and later appli- cation of digestate could thus result in more efficient nutrient use by the crops and lower emissions to the environment. To enable continuous operation of a biogas plant, a storage solution is needed to preserve the cover crop biomass until it can be fed to the biogas reac- tor. nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What type of fertilizer was applied at the rate of 5130 kg ha⁻¹ per year?
nodes.answer: Cow dung was applied as manure fertilizer at the rate of 5130 kg ha⁻¹ per year.
nodes.paragraph: Cow dung was applied at the rate of 5130 kg ha 1 per year as manure fertilizer. The previous sea- son S crop straw was used for the straw application. Detailed nitrogen, phosphorous, and potassium nutrient inputs for each treatment are provided in Table S1. Application of manure and straw were performed follow - ing the crop harvest in the Autumn. Diammonium phos- phate and potassium sulphate, along with 50% of the N fertilizer (the N shortage was replenished by urea), were applied before sowing in the Spring. The remaining N fer - tilizer as urea was applied at the bolting stage. A popular sorghum cultivar, Jinza 31, was seeded with a plant den- sity of 120,0 plant ha 1 in April 2020, and harvested in September 2020. The growing season experienced no obvi- ous issues with pests, diseases, or weed infestations. Soils attached to the surface of five sorghum plant roots were col - lected at the jointing, heading, filling and maturity stages in 2020 as rhizosphere soils. The rhizosphere soil samples were immediately taken to the laboratory and sieved soils to < 2 mm, and stored at 80 C for molecular analyses.

nodes.question: What type of nitrogen fertilizer was applied to the plots, and how much was used each year?
nodes.answer: Solid pellets of urea were applied to the plots, totaling 100 kg N ha⁻¹ per year, with 50 kg N ha⁻¹ applied in April and late June.
nodes.paragraph: Fertilized plots received nitrogen as solid pellets of urea in April and in late June each year for a total of 100 kg N ha 1 y 1 (50 kg N ha 1 per application), corresponding to the amount of fertilizer proposed for mid-intensive to intensive grasslands of Switzerland 51. The fungicides Score Profi (24.8% difenoconazole; Syngenta Agro AG, Basel, Switzerland) and Ortiva (22.8% azoxystrobin; Syngenta Agro GmbH, Maintal, Germany) were applied each year four times during the growing period (0.2 mL of Score Profi and 0.4 mL of Ortiva mixed with 0.62 L of water per plot and time). Plots without fungicide application were sprayed with the same amount of water. Functional composition was manipulated by dividing the 20 sown species into ten fast- and ten slow-growing species (Table S1). Communities were then established with either only fast-, only slow-growing strategies, or both fast and slow strategies. To maintain the original sown vascular plant species richness and composition, one part of each plot (1.5 m m) was weeded, while the other part was left unweeded since the beginning of the experiment (0.5 m 2 m).
